title: Osprey Farpoint 40 long-term review: 18 months, 19 countries — TrailToTerminal
text: Eighteen months in, the Farpoint 40 remains the pack I recommend to anyone who walks. The suspension is the whole story: the ventilated back panel keeps your shirt dry in Lisbon summer, and the hipbelt genuinely carries 70-80% of the load — I tracked 60,000-step weeks with zero shoulder pain. Load lifters let you pull the mass tight on stairs. The stowaway harness zips away clean for gate checks. Downsides after heavy use: it is 1.6 kg empty, noticeable on a scale-obsessed budget airline; the 55 x 35 x 25 frame will not fold into a Ryanair sizer no matter how you push; and at $185 it is a real purchase. One seam started lifting at month 14 — Osprey's All Mighty Guarantee repaired it free in 12 days, which converts skeptics into lifers. Verdict: for long walking days and heavy loads there is still nothing at this price that carries better.
